originality.rationale: Full primary text of Xu–Han–Jiang (arXiv:math/0509202v1) studies cohomology of the same truncated quiver algebras but not elementwise regular-module Jordan type. Accessible Dugas–Huisgen-Zimmermann–Learned and Babson–Huisgen-Zimmermann–Thomas abstracts address projective dimensions and generic representations, not a displayed operator-count theorem; these inaccessible full-text implications remain a risk. Comparisons against earlier mathematical claims and a published mathematical-finding index did not identify an equivalent or stronger enumeration. Existing square-zero-cycle and radical-square-zero results do not imply this length-three linear-quiver transfer matrix.

value.rationale: A canonical finite-dimensional representation, left multiplication on the regular module, has a natural but previously unaccounted joint rank distribution for all radical elements. The all-degree, all-finite-field transfer matrix resolves every nilpotent Jordan partition multiplicity, while its square-zero specialization is an exact independent-set weighted count. The result yields substantially more than an isolated computation and does not rely on conjectured downstream implications.
